note: Rule register. Every rule is re-run by tools/probe.py (and by tools/validate.py --tests). outcome: CONFIRMED = discriminating evidence for the statement; CONSISTENT_NOT_DISCRIMINATED = everything matched so far is compatible, but no experiment has yet shown the alternative fails; FALSIFIED = evidence against.

rules.statement: All three episodes were linked with the Turbo C 2.0 large-model startup: C0L.OBJ _TEXT equals image bytes [0,455) outside its own fixups in DN1/DN2/DN3; C0S/C0T/C0C/C0M/C0H all differ.

TASM 1.0 (/D__LARGE__ /MX) reassembles the shipped STARTUP\C0.ASM to the same _TEXT bytes, fixups and publics as the shipped C0L.OBJ, so a C0 variant with appended assembly (the region [0x1C9,0x603) shared by all episodes) is buildable from source with the pinned assembler. The game's own C0 variant is NOT yet reconstructed.
64 Turbo C 2.0 CL.LIB code segments (12,845 bytes) occur exactly once, byte-exact outside their fixups, in each episode; library code is CL.LIB (large model).

LZEXE 0.91 stores relocations as ascending deltas with paragraph-normalised offsets, so the original TLINK relocation table order and seg:off split are not recoverable from DN?.EXE; acceptance compares relocation sets only.
-O (jump optimisation) is in effect for G1/G2 C code: without it the canonical pilots grow jump chains (jmp $+2) and stop matching.
-K (char is unsigned) is in effect: without it char loads gain cbw and compares widen.
-G (optimise for speed) is in effect: 2-byte caller cleanup is 'inc sp; inc sp' instead of 'pop cx'.
-1- (8086 instructions) is in effect: with -1 (80186) 'push imm' replaces 'mov ax,imm; push ax' and g1_006f stops matching.
-Z (register load suppression) is part of the external Duke1Decomp profile. No accepted function yet changes when -Z is removed; status stays open until a discriminating function is matched.
Object-level: with -Z, 'a = b; c = b;' stores AX twice without reloading b; without -Z it reloads. Pattern to look for when hunting a -Z discriminator in the original code.

Large model, one translation unit: calls to externals are relocated far calls (EXTDEF fixup); calls to functions defined earlier, and to static functions even when only forward-declared, are 'push cs; call near' resolved at compile time (no fixup); calls to public functions defined later are far calls with an own-segment fixup. Consequence: in the original, backward far calls inside one segment never occur (verified: 0 in G1 and G2) and forward 'push cs; call near' (197 in G1) indicate static functions.
Functions ending in 'retf N' are pascal: g1_e92e matches only when declared pascal (callers then do no stack cleanup, cf. g1_006f calling g2_1f5a).
